manual: Experimental Instruction Manual: Rubber Eraser vs Metal Block Sliding Down Identical RampsI. Basic Experiment InformationExperiment Title: Comparison of Sliding Motion of Rubber Eraser and Metal Block on Identical RampsSubject: Physics – Mechanics (Friction)Objective: To observe the effect of friction on motion by comparing the sliding behavior of a rubber eraser and a metal block on identical inclined planes.II. Experimental EquipmentTwo identical ramps, rubber eraser, metal block, adjustable support (to change ramp angle), flat table surface.III. Experimental Procedure1. Place two identical ramps side by side on a flat table, ensuring equal length and surface material.2. Put the rubber eraser at the top of the left ramp and the metal block at the top of the right ramp.3. Ensure both objects are initially at rest and aligned at the same height.4. Slowly and simultaneously increase the angle of both ramps using the adjustable support.5. Continue increasing the angle until one or both objects begin to slide, then stop adjusting and observe.IV. Observation of Experimental Phenomena1. At small angles, neither object slides.2. As the angle increases, the metal block begins to slide down first.3. The rubber eraser remains stationary until a larger angle is reached, then slides more slowly.V. Summary of Experimental PrincipleThis experiment demonstrates the effect of friction on motion. The rubber eraser experiences greater friction with the ramp surface than the metal block. A larger component of gravitational force (from a steeper angle) is required to overcome this friction, so the eraser starts sliding later than the metal block.
high_level_evaluation_guide: Target concept: friction affects the onset of sliding on an inclined plane, with different materials having different coefficients of friction. Minimum assumptions: identical ramps, same gravitational field, and synchronized angle adjustment. Expected phenomena storyline: (1) Both objects rest on shallow ramps; (2) angle increases together, increasing downslope gravitational component; (3) metal block overcomes friction first and slides; (4) rubber eraser resists longer due to higher friction, then slides at a steeper angle. Visibility constraints: left-right placement must be clear, angle change must be observable, and relative motion timing must be distinguishable within a short, accelerated demonstration.
